sources.handbook: Cornell Engineering Undergraduate Handbook Fall 2025, EAS pp. 66-70 (notes e, g, i, j)
sources.page: https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/eas/degree/earth-atmospheric-sciences-bs-requirements/ (served as "B.S. in Earth and Climate Sciences", 2026 site; same page at /eas/degree/earth-climate-sciences-bs/)

pageRules: Electives must be approved by the student's faculty advisor. One Major-approved elective at the 3000 level or above. Three outside Major Electives. Two Advisor-approved electives. (handbook p.67)
One Advisor-approved course in statistics, computer science, math, or natural science (handbook p.66, notes b and f)

f. An Advisor-approved course in statistics, computer science, mathematics, or natural science (including, but not limited to, a course in astronomy, a second course in biology, or an additional course in physics or chemistry).

b. If a student elects to count CS 1110 (or CS 1112) as their Major-required, Advisor-approved course in statistics, computer science, math, or natural science, an additional Major-approved elective is required.
g. Three core courses depending on the concentration (Fall 2025 handbook)

The concentration is achieved by completing five intermediate- to advanced-level courses (3000 level or above) ... See department website for current list of approved concentration courses for each concentration. Courses not on the list must be approved by the student's advisor and Director of Undergraduate Studies. A minimum of 15 credits of concentration courses is required.

Field Course (at least 3 credits): EAS 2500, EAS 4370, Courses in SEA Semester, field courses offered at Shoals Marine Laboratory*, field courses offered by another college or university*, field research with Cornell faculty (or REU)*, 3 credits of independent research. (* pre-approval by the faculty advisor and the EAS Curriculum Committee)
j. The Major program includes nine (9) credits of courses outside the Major.
Engineering Communications ... may be taken as a liberal studies or Advisor-Approved Elective.

biologyAlso.why: Kept from the existing program list: the individualized-instruction section of BIOG 1440 (catalog title 'Introduction to Comparative Anatomy and Physiology, Individualized Instruction').

advisorCourse.why: Note f: statistics, computer science, mathematics or natural science (astronomy, biology, physics, chemistry named). Any level; 3+ credits, the seat's minimum.
advisorCourse.exceptWhy: College rule (handbook p.23): no course numbered below 1100 counts, nor courses that precede where the Engineering curriculum begins, 'such as CS 1109 or MATH 1110'; the Fall 2026 handbook also names MATH 1900.
advisorCourse.excludeWhy: Note f asks for a course in a science. Research, thesis and independent-study credit is left out (an advisor may still approve it); this also keeps EAS 4910/4920 free for the field course's research option.
